The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 and requested this Court to set aside the Arbitral Award dated 22.01.2021 passed in case No.LAQ/ARB/NH- 07/CR/72/2012-13.
.2.
In the petition it is stated that, National Highways Authority of India was constituted by an Act the Parliament, "The National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988".

entities.text: National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is stated that, the Central A.P. No.131/2021 Government for the purpose of widening/upgradation, maintenance management and operation of NH-7 on the stretch of land from Kms 524.720 Kms. 556.840 of Hyderabad - Bangalore Section issued preliminary notification dated 09/12/2009.

Final notification bearing S.O.
No. 1622(E) under section 3-D(1) & (2) of the NH Act was published in the official Gazette on 02/07/2010.

It is stated that, for 2 nd state of acquisition, amongst other lands the agricultural (dry)
lands in Sy. No. 17/A to an extent of 45.70 Sq.Mtrs situated at the said village belonging to the 1 st respondent were also acquired.

It is stated that, the respondent No. 3 was appointed as the competent Authority by the Central Government to perform task related to acquisition of land for the project including hearing of objections, deciding on the same, determination of compensation and releasing of the same.
The 3rd Respondent vide award dated 24/05/2011 determined the market value of agricultural lands at Rs. 2,26,48,783/- per acre.

The 3 rd A.P. No.131/2021 respondent obtained the sale statistics for the period 08/12/2008 to 09/12/2009 as well as the guidance values for the relevant period of the said village from the office of the Sub-Registrar,
Bangalore North Taluk.

Since the guidance value was on a lesser side, the 3 rd respondent relied upon the average of the sale statistics fixed the market value of agricultural lands at Rs.
2,26,48,783/- per acre.

It is stated that, being dissatisfied with the amount awarded by respondent No. 3, respondent belatedly approached the 2 nd respondent under section 3-G (5) of the NH Act who is appointed as the Arbitrator.
The petitioner entered appearance and filed its statement of objections with document as well as written submissions with several judgments in support of its defence.

The respondent redetermined the market at Rs. 5,25,00,000/- per acre equivalent to Rs.
12,973/- per Sq. Mtr.
.3.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner has preferred this petition on the following grounds:

sentences.text: ( 1) It is stated that, the impugned Arbitral award passed by the 2nd respondent is perverse, patently illegal capricious.
(2) The respondent has grossly erred in not following the provisions of NH Act.
It is stated that, the 2nd respondent has not complied with the provision of Section 28 of the A & C Act, therefore it is patently illegal and requires to be set aside.

(3) The 2nd respondent has not made any attempt to investigate the market value of the subject lands as on the date of publication of preliminary Notification; it is relevant to mentioned that the said notification has come into effect from 26.09.2011 while the date of preliminary notification in the case of subject acquisition in Venkatala Village was 09/12/2009.
Hence, the 2nd respondent could not have relied upon a notification which came into effect after a lapse of 1 year from the date of publication of preliminary notification.

(4) Taking the said guidance value as the basis, the 2nd respondent further at page 6 of the impugned Arbitral award has added a percentage of 50 of the guidance value of Rs. 3 crores on the ground that the special instruction to the aforesaid notification provides for the addition of 50% for such lands abutting National Highways.

nd Thereafter, the 2 respondent has once again added a percent of 25 on the guidance without assigning any reasons and arrived at Rs. 5,25,00,000/- per acre.
A.P. No.131/2021 (5)
The 2nd respondent himself has stated at page 5 of the impugned Arbitral award the guidance value of lands abutting National Highway was Rs. 3 Crores per acre.
Even assuming for the sake of arguments that the 2nd respondent could have relied upon said notification, still he could have awarded only Rs. 3 crores per acre.
Instead, the 2nd respondent has awarded a further percentage of 50 by holding that the same was provided under the special instructions to the Notification dated 21/07/2011.
(6) The additional percentage has to be added only for such properties abutting National Highway which were not included in the list.
When the Notification itself provided for guidance value of lands abutting NH.
The question of adding any further percentage would not at all arise.
(7) That several arbitration cases pertaining to Kadiganahalli village which is just at a distance of 7 kms.
From Venkatala were disposed of by the very same Arbitrator wherein the market value of agricultural lands was fixed as Rs. 3 crores per acre by the 3rd respondent.

Since Kadaginahalli Village is near to Venkatala Village, having exactly same guidance value fixed under same notification, which has been relied upon by the 2nd respondent, he could not have ignored the said rate and further added 75% on the same is arbitrary manner.

(8) The notification dated 21/09/2011 is a document which did not form a part of the A.P.
No.131/2021 Arbitral Proceedings and the petitioner was never given an opportunity to rebut the same.
The impugned Arbitral award is contrary to provisions of Section 24 of the A & C Act.

sentences.text: (9) The respondent has given the benefit of enhancement to the 1st respondent with production by the 1st respondent of any records or evidence in support of such enhancement which is completely arbitrary.

(10) The 2nd respondent has neither complied with the procedure provided under section 24, not decided the dispute in accordance with section 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with section 31(3) of the A & C Act, thus rendering the impugned Arbitral award opposed to settled position of law.
(11) The petitioner submits that the impugned Arbtral Award was passed on 22/01/2021.
The certified copy of the Arbitral award was received by the petitioner on 09/02/2021.
The stipulated period of 3 months commences from 09/02/2021 and expired on 09/05/2021.
In continuation of the previous order, the Hon'ble Supreme court vide its order dated 27/04/2021 has also excluded the period from 14/03/2021 for the purpose of computation of limitation period.

Hence the petition is in time.
.4.
The respondents have not filed objections.
.5. Heard.

.6. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
(1) Whether the petitioner proves any of the grounds mentioned under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, to set aside the award passed by the learned Arbitrator?
( 2 ) What order or award?

.7. My findings on the above points are:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative, Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .8. POINT No.1: Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 provide the circumstances under which an award can be set aside by a civil Court.

Explanation 2. The test as to whether there is contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian law shall not entail a review on the merits of the dispute.

It may also be set aside if the Court finds the award is vitiated by patent illegality appearing on the face of award provided that an award shall not be set aside merely on the ground of an erroneous application of law or by re appreciation of evidence.

.9. In Kwality Manufacturing Corporation Vs. Central Whorehouse Corporation (2009) 5 Sec.142, it has been held that:
"From catena of other judgments of this Court, it is clear that for the objector /
appellant in order to succeed in their challenge against an arbitral award, they must show that the award of the Arbitrator suffered from perversity or an error of law or that the Arbitrator has otherwise misconducted himself.

Bearing in mind the above section and decision, now it has to be seen whether the impugned award suffers from any patent error, illegality as envisaged above.
The land bearing Sy.No. 17/1A of Venkatala village measuring to an extent of 45.70 sq. meters was acquired under preliminary notification dated 09.12.2009.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs. 2,26,48,783/- per acre.
Being aggrieved by the said award, the respondent No. 1 had preferred Arbitration Petition before the respondent No. 2 and the respondent No. 2 had re-

determined the market value at the rate of Rs. 5,25,00,000/- per acre = Rs. 12,973/-
per sq. meters.
.11.
The petitioner has stated that the Arbitrator has relied upon the notification dated 21.09.2011.
The preliminary notification in the present case was issued on 09.12.2009 and award was passed much prior to the notification dated 26.09.2011.

It is stated that the respondent could not have relied upon notification, which came into effect after lapse of more than 21 months from the date of National Highway Authority Of India vs ) Smt. M.Kumari on 16 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65204019/

sentences.text: As per the Substantive Law NH Authority Act Section 3-G(7)(a) the Arbitrator while determining the A.P. No.131/2021 amount shall take into consideration the market value of the land as on the date of publication of the notification under Section 3-A of NH Act.
The respondent No. 2 could not have relied upon the notification which came into effect after lapse of 21 months from the date of preliminary notification.

.13 . The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd., Vs. SAW Pipes Ltd. (AIR 2003 SC 2629) has held that:
 "if the award is contrary to the  Substantive provisions of law or the provisions of the Act or against the terms of the contract, it would be patently illegal, which could be interfered under Section 34".

The Arbitrator relying upon guidance value dated 26.09.2011 has fixed the market value at Rs. 5 crores 25 lakhs per acre or Rs. 12,973/- per sq. meter.

It is clear that the respondent No. 2 Arbitrator has ignored the Substantive Law under Section 3-G(7)(a) of National A.P. No.131/2021 Highways Authority Act and thereby the provisions of Section 28 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act while passing the impugned award.

sentences.text: Therefore, the award is patently illegal.
.14. The Arbitrator has relied upon estimated market value of the immovable properties and buildings for registration in Bengaluru dated 21.09.2011.
This document is not valid record received from the Arbitrator as none of the parties have produced and this is evident from the record of the Arbitrator.
Section 24(3) of the Act provides provision regarding hearing and written proceedings.

It reads thus:
"All statements, documents or other information supplied to, or applications made to the aribral tribunal by one party shall be communicated to the other party, and any expert report or evidentiary document on which the arbital tribunal may rely in making its decision shall be communicated to the parties".
A.P. No.131/2021 .15.

As Arbitrator has relied on the estimated market value of immovable properties and buildings dated 21.09.2011 for Registration in Bengaluru without bringing to the knowledge of the parties and thereby has failed to follow the procedure under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
So there is patent illegality.

.16. The petitioner has contended that the respondent No. 2 has not assigned any reasons for re- determining the compensation amount at Rs.5,25,00,000/- per acre i.e., Rs. 3 crores + Rs.1 crore 50 lakhs per acre (50% of Rs. 3 crores) + Rs. 75 lakhs ( 25% of Rs. 5,25,00,000/- per acre).
It is stated that he has not assigned any reasons for enhancing the compensation or for relying upon notification dated 21.09.2011.

As per the instructions to the notification, the instruction No. 3 has National Highway Authority Of India vs ) Smt. M.Kumari on 16 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65204019/
6 stated that the lands which are not included in the list of properties which were attached to National Highways and State Highways more value of 50% and 25% of the prescribed value A.P. No.131/2021 shall be levied.

sentences.text: So, the additional percentage has to be added only for such properties abutting National Highways which were not included in the list.
In the present case the guidance value of Sy.No. 17 was specifically provided in page No. 464 Sl. No. 132 of the said notification which was adjacent to National Highways as Rs. 3 crores per acre.
The question of adding any further percentage of 50 + 25 would not arise.
There is an error apparent on the face of record, which would render the imugned Arbitral Award patently illegal.

.17. In Som Dutt Builders Ltd Vs. State of Kerala (2010)2 AWC (supp) 1390 SC) has held that:
"Reasons must be indicated in the award as that would reflect thought process leading to a particular conclusion.

sentences.text: To satisfy the requirement of Section 31(3), the reasons must be stated by the Arbitral Tribunal upon which the award is based; want of reasons would make such award legally flawed."

On perusal of the records and the award of the Arbitrator it is seen that the respondent No.2 has neither complied with the procedure provided under Section 24 nor decided the dispute in accordance with Section 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with Section 31(3) of the A & C Act, thus rendering the impugned Arbitral Award opposed to settled position of law.

.19. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd. Vs. SAW Piles Ltd., (AIR 2003 SC 2629) has held that:
"if the award is patently against the statutory provisions or Substantive law which is in force in India or is passed without giving an opportunity of hearing to the parties as provided under Section 24 or without giving any reason in a case where parties have not agreed that no reasons are to be recorded

In all such cases, the award is required to be set aside on the ground of 'patent illegality' A.P. No.131/2021
The above decision applies to the case on hand.

.20. The Arbitrator has not taken into consideration additional market value of 12%,
30% solatium and 15% interest on additional market value and solatium.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has in AIR 2019 SC 4689: AIR Online 2019 SC 1087 - Union of India and another Vs. Tarsem Singh and others has held that:
"provisions of Land Acquisition Act relating to solatium and interest contained in S.23(1A) and (2) and interest payable in terms of Section 28 proviso - will apply to acquisitions made under National Highways Act - Consequently, S. 3-J to extent of granting compensation without solatium and interest - Is violative of Art. 14 of Constitution and, therefore, declared to be unconstitutional.
